images.title: Four calendar years
images.purpose: Show that 4 calendar years with one leap day make 1461 days, a little more than the 1460.9688 days of 4 Earth revolutions.
images.composition: Two horizontal bars stacked in the middle of the frame, calendar on top and Earth below, left ends aligned, with a small highlighted overhang at the right end of the top bar and white space above and below.
exact_structure: Top bar, the calendar: 4 equal width blocks side by side, left to right
Label to the right of the top bar: '4 × 365 + 1 = 1461 days'
Bottom bar, the Earth: 1 single green #009E73 bar starting at the same left edge, ending very slightly before the right end of the top bar
Label to the right of the bottom bar: '4 × 365.2422 = 1460.9688 days'
1 small reddish purple #CC79A7 bracket marking the sliver where the top bar overhangs the bottom bar, labelled 'Calendar ahead by 0.0312 day'
rejection: the top bar having a number of blocks other than 4, or more than one amber 366 block
the Earth bar drawn longer than the calendar bar
images.takeaway: A leap day every 4 years slightly overshoots: the calendar runs ahead of the Earth by 0.0312 day every 4 years.
images.description: A bar of four year blocks, 365, 365, 365 and 366, totalling 1461 days above a slightly shorter Earth bar of 1460.9688 days, with the 0.0312 day overhang marked.
images.context: Shown beside the concept text and video on adding a leap day every 4 years.
images.teaching_notes: Compare the two bar ends and ask which is longer before reading the difference.

image_decisions.why: Two aligned bars make the tiny overcompensation of the 4 year rule visible.
